description: Thresholds for the local conditional hypothesis Brain. Every value here is a development default chosen so the five lifecycle operations are reachable on a short replay; none has been fitted or validated against out-of-sample outcomes.

trajectory.identity: the ATR-normalized cumulative return curve, projected onto a globally fitted principal basis. Realized volatility is an attribute and never an identity dimension.

proposer._minimum_mass_note: The share of the retrieved neighbourhood a cluster needs before it is surfaced as a representative future. Mass below this is left to the residual rather than named.
proposer._cluster_count_note: How finely the retrieved neighbourhood is cut before the top nodes by mass are kept. Chosen from study_cluster_selection on 2022-01-03/04/05 against 2022-01-07/10/11: k=4 had the highest block-resample stability (0.840) and the lowest reproduction distance among k>=3. Note this is the LOCAL cut of ~200 neighbours, while the sweep cut the whole window, so the sweep informs the resolution rather than fixing it. Centroid shapes reproduced poorly at every k (0.50 at k=2 falling to 0.17 at k=6), which is a three-day-window result and not a settled one.
proposer._max_nodes_note: How many representative futures the cloud surfaces, deliberately larger than pool.max_live_hypotheses. A SPLIT is made of a node the pool has no slot for yet; capping extraction at the number of slots makes it unreachable by construction.

pool._association_note: association_max_distance_scale is a fraction of the principal basis's own spread (ForecastIndex.component_scale), not an absolute distance: PC coordinates scale with the window's volatility, so a fixed number would mean something different in every regime. Measured on 2022-01-03/04/05, consecutive-clock centroid matches had a median distance of 0.17 scales; 0.5 admits about three quarters of them. Nothing here is calibrated.
